$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.query.cli. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-CLI-UNKNOWN-NO-PLURAL-PROBE
arms.find: return direct.length > 0 || !name.endsWith('s') ? direct : CliWalk.findFuzzy(name.substr(0, name.length - 1), pool);
arms.note: the singular-stem retry is dropped, so `apq members` is five edits and no substring away from every real command and the unknown-subcommand notice offers nothing - the exact miss the notice replaced the whole help page to answer

arms.name: M-CLI-COMMANDS-MEMOISED
arms.note: the registry memoises its command objects into process-scoped state, so every run of the CLI shares one instance of each command

arms.name: M-POST-WRITE-FIX-HULL
arms.note: a write op's --fix lints the whole file instead of the lines the write changed, so a standing finding between or around two edited regions is rewritten too

arms.name: M-POST-WRITE-FIX-TRIVIA-BLIND
arms.note: no line reads as trivia, so a write that changed only a comment still applies code fixes anchored on that comment line

arms.name: M-POST-WRITE-FIX-FAIL-OPEN
arms.replace: if (edits == null) return [{ from: 1, to: now.length }];
arms.note: a diff past its budget falls back to one window over the whole file, so a write op's --fix rewrites code the write never touched

arms.name: M-CLI-REQUIREMATCH-STATIC
arms.note: the per-run flag gains a static backing, so one invocation's --exit-on-empty survives into the next one in the same process

arms.name: M-PROGRESS-TTY-BLIND
arms.find: return progressEnv != null && progressEnv != '' ? progressEnv != '0' : !noProgressSet && stderrTty;
arms.note: the pre-slice rule is back — the heartbeat prints into a pipe unless HXQ_NO_PROGRESS is set, so 38 stderr lines land in a transcript per src-wide walk again

arms.name: M-BATCH-SEPARATOR-BLIND
arms.note: a bare `--` stops splitting queries from scope, so `refs A B -- src` reads A as the one name and B as a scope spec and every batch collapses to its first query

arms.name: M-KIND-GATE-FAIL-OPEN
arms.note: the shared --kind vocabulary gate calls every kind known again, so `apq lit 'x' F.hx --kind Literaal` goes back to printing `0 hits` at exit 0 - a typo answering exactly like a scope that genuinely holds no match

arms.name: M-WRITE-DIR-UNCREATED
arms.note: a write into a missing directory no longer creates it

arms.name: M-WRITE-DIR-KEPT
arms.note: a change set that is not written keeps the directories it created

arms.name: M-PICK-PLUGIN-FOR-IGNORES-PATH
arms.note: the file's extension is ignored, so the `--lang haxe` the shim prepends parses a `.json` file as Haxe and every JSON edit is refused

arms.name: M-CODE-CACHE-KEY-IGNORES-SOURCE
arms.note: the key no longer hashes the engine's content, so a same-length rebuild is offered the old cache and V8, which checks only the length, runs the old engine's top level

arms.name: M-CODE-CACHE-KEY-IGNORES-RUNTIME
arms.note: the key no longer carries node, V8 and flags, so a cache filed under another runtime is read as this one's

arms.name: M-CODE-CACHE-NO-CHECKSUM
arms.note: the payload checksum is not verified, so a cache damaged after its header is handed to V8, which does not verify it either and can abort on it

arms.name: M-CODE-CACHE-WRITE-IN-PLACE
arms.find:
Fs.writeFileSync(temp, Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(MAGIC, 'latin1'), key, sha256(payload), payload]));
			Fs.renameSync(temp, path);
arms.note: the cache is rewritten in place instead of renamed over, so a reader at the same time can see half a file

arms.name: M-CODE-CACHE-PERSIST-IGNORES-STAMP
arms.note: a run of an engine rewritten on disk since it was read still saves its cache, replacing the one a fresh build just warmed

arms.name: M-CODE-CACHE-KEY-IGNORES-PATH
arms.note: the key no longer carries the engine's real path, so a cache copied beside another copy of the engine is read there and every stack names the copy it was written from

arms.name: M-CODE-CACHE-KEY-IGNORES-EXECPATH
arms.note: the tag no longer names the node binary, so two node builds of one version string but different V8 configuration share a cache whose payload verifies and can still abort the other

arms.name: M-MODMOVE-CLI-ORIGINAL-KEPT
arms.note: a written relocation leaves the original module in place

arms.name: M-SCOPE-FILES-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: a named file the scope walk holds under another spelling is indexed twice

arms.name: M-MODMOVE-CLI-TEXT-ROOT-MISSING
arms.note: a declared text root that does not exist is skipped in silence

arms.name: M-DECLARATION-DELTA-BY-POSITION
arms.note: declarations are paired by position instead of by name, so a member inserted in the middle reports every member below it as changed

arms.name: M-DECLARATION-DELTA-RECORDS-IN-ORDER
arms.note: records sharing a name path pair up in order without first matching identical ones, so a record inserted first reports every record after it as changed

arms.name: M-DECLARATION-DELTA-BODY-FILTERED
arms.note: a body line of punctuation alone no longer counts, so a closing brace moved past a statement reads as no change and the file falls through to imports or renamed

arms.name: M-DECLARATION-DELTA-RENAME-UNBOUND
arms.note: every spelling of a renamed name counts as its binding, so a member renamed beside a same-named call on another receiver reads as a rename

arms.name: M-DECLARATION-DELTA-BODY-TRIMMED
arms.note: body lines are compared trimmed and without punctuation-only lines, so a closing brace moved past a statement beside an added import reads as an imports-only change

arms.name: M-GET-STRING-QUOTED
arms.note: `apq get` prints a string value as a quoted, escaped JSON literal instead of its decoded text, so a script reading a key gets the quotes and backslashes too

arms.name: M-DATA-PATH-ESCAPE-IGNORED
arms.note: a backslash-escaped dot in a path splits like any other, so a key that holds a dot can no longer be named

arms.name: M-LANG-OF-FILE-NONE
arms.note: no extension names a grammar, so every process call without `--lang` is refused even on a `.json` or `.hx` file

arms.name: M-LANG-OF-CONTENT-NONE
arms.note: a JSON document on stdin is no longer recognised by its content, so `cat x.json | apq get - k` needs `--lang`

arms.name: M-LANG-CHOICE-FLAG-VALUE-COUNTED
arms.note: no flag takes a value, so a value such as `sweep --save base.json` reads as a file naming the grammar

arms.name: M-LANG-PRESET-OVERRIDES
arms.note: a preset's grammar overrides the file extensions, so `hxq fmt arms.json` reads JSON as Haxe and fails with a parse error

arms.name: M-LANG-PRESET-IGNORED
arms.note: `--lang-default` is dropped unread, so every `hxq` call on a directory or an extension no grammar registers becomes a usage error

arms.name: M-LANG-PRESET-MIXED-REFUSED
arms.note: files of two grammars are refused under a preset too, so `hxq lint F.hx apq.json` exits 2 where it read both as Haxe

arms.name: M-LANG-END-OF-OPTIONS-VALUE
arms.note: `--` reads as a flag taking a value, so the first path after it names no grammar and a call picks the grammar of the paths after

arms.name: M-GET-WALKABLE-ALWAYS
arms.note: a grammar with no object or array kind (mermaid) is walked anyway, so `apq get x.mmd a` no longer says the grammar has no path to name

arms.name: M-GRAPH-DIFF-ABSOLUTE-SPEC-UNREAD
arms.note: an absolute scope is compared with the cwd-relative paths git lists and names nothing at either revision

arms.name: M-GIT-REVISION-SPEC-UNRESOLVED
arms.note: an absolute scope gone from the disk keeps its linked spelling while the cwd is resolved, so git is handed a path outside the repository

arms.name: M-CLI-FLAGS-SWITCH-TAKES-VALUE
arms.note: every long flag reads as taking a value, so `fmt --list A.hx b.json` drops A.hx and formats a Haxe file as JSON

arms.name: M-CLI-UNKNOWN-FLAG-ADMITTED
arms.note: an undeclared `--word` passes the dispatcher, so each command's own parser decides whether it is refused, read as a path, or swallowed

arms.name: M-CLI-OPTIONAL-VALUE-NEVER-TAKEN
arms.note: an optional-value flag never takes the token after it, so `add-element F.hx --after 3:4 x` reads the position as the code

arms.name: M-CLI-SEPARATOR-ALWAYS-ADMITTED
arms.note: every spec admits a bare `--`, so `fmt --list -- F.hx` runs and a parser with no `--` arm drops it silently

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-NO-ROLLBACK
arms.note: a write that turns a green build red is replayed and kept, so the op exits 0 over a tree that no longer compiles

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-RED-BEFORE-JUDGES
arms.note: a build red before the write counts as broken by it, so a write into a project that never compiled is always put back

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-UNREACHED-KEPT
arms.note: a created module no configured build compiles, even when named to it, stays on disk as unverified

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-COUNTS-EVERY-BUILD
arms.note: every green build vouches for the write, including one that never parsed a written file

arms.name: M-WRITE-JOURNAL-NO-RECORD
arms.note: the run records none of its writes, so nothing is verified and a rollback restores nothing

arms.name: M-WRITE-JOURNAL-DIRS-KEPT
arms.note: a rollback deletes the files the run created but leaves the directories it made for them

arms.name: M-WRITE-JOURNAL-NO-RESTORE
arms.note: a rollback leaves every file as the run wrote it, so a write the build rejects stays on disk

arms.name: M-WRITE-JOURNAL-SEAT-KEPT
arms.note: a run whose body throws leaves its journal recording, so every later write in the process lands in a finished run's journal

arms.name: M-WRITE-JOURNAL-PLAIN-KEY
arms.note: the journal keys a file by its spelling, so a second spelling records the text the run already wrote as its original and a rollback restores that

arms.name: M-WRITE-SAME-TARGET-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: a change set is keyed by the spelling of each path, so one file named twice through a symlink or a dot segment passes the refusal and half-writes the set

arms.name: M-WRITE-JOURNAL-MODE-LOST
arms.note: a rolled-back deletion restores the file with the default mode, so an executable script comes back 0644

arms.name: M-FLOW-CLI-BRANCHES-IGNORED
arms.note: a member declared once per conditional-compilation branch is drawn from its first declaration alone, the others unmentioned

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-HOLDERS-COMPILE
arms.note: a run that only created modules compiles no build as configured, so a module a build reads only through its own folder walk, a shadow or a lookup is vouched for by a build that never reads it

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-ONLY-HOLDERS
arms.note: a run that only created modules compiles every configured build, including one whose class paths hold none of them

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-BLAMED-CREATED-NO-ROLLBACK-COMPILE
arms.note: a red build whose errors blame a created module is compiled again without the write, and a build red before it judges nothing

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-ONE-HOLDER-NOT-FINAL
arms.note: the first build that rejects a created module puts the run back, though a larger build holding the module's dependencies would typecheck it

arms.name: M-WRITE-VERIFY-STOPS-AT-FIRST-GREEN
arms.note: a created module a cheap holder typechecks is named to the other holders as well, one compile each
